## In one sentence

Organisms persist where environmental conditions and resources remain within the
limits required for survival and reproduction.

## Conditions and resources

Conditions are environmental features an organism tolerates, such as
 temperature, pH, salinity, or flow. Resources are consumed or used, such as
water, nutrients, light, space, or prey. A factor can be a condition at one
scale and a resource at another.

## Tolerance and performance

For many factors, performance is highest within an optimum range and declines
toward lower and upper tolerance limits. The law of the minimum says that growth
can be limited by the scarcest essential resource relative to demand. In
practice, multiple factors interact, so one limiting factor can change as the
environment changes.

A species response curve is a useful first model:

$$
\text{performance} = f(\text{environmental factor})
$$

The curve should be estimated rather than assumed to be symmetric or constant
through time.

## Climate and microclimate

Climate describes long-term regional patterns; microclimate describes the local
conditions an organism actually experiences. Shade, soil depth, canopy cover,
and shelter can make microclimate differ strongly from weather-station data.

## Check your understanding

Choose one species and draw its expected performance across a temperature
 gradient. Add a second factor and explain why the first curve might shift.
